newsitem.title: USA: Irving Oil, Maine settle alleged labor violations.
newsitem.headline: Irving Oil, Maine settle alleged labor violations.

text.p: Irving Oil Corp has agreed to pay more than $77,000 to the state of Maine to settle allegations of child labor violations at its company gas stations and restaurants.
In an announcement Wednesday the state attorney general's office said the Maine oil company agreed on Tuesday to pay $77,852 to settle the case.
The case involved more than 800 alleged violations of state limits on curfew and the number of hours that minors under the age of 18 are allowed to work.
The violations allegedly occurred last year at 33 of the company's about 93 locations in Maine. The company also markets petroleum products in New Hampshire and Vermont.

"We take child labor violations very seriuosly," said Alan Hinsey, of Maine's Department of Labor. "We can never give back the lost hours to those young people, and we can't undo the harm that working inapproprite hours may have done..."
Hinsey and the state said they were satisfied with Irving's actions to correct the alleged violations and to prevent others from occurring.

According to Maine law, minors under the age of 18 cannot work more than 20 hours a week when school is in session, or 50 hours a week when school is closed. They also cannot work more than 10 hours a day or beyond 10 p.m. on a school day.
The laws are more stringent for those under 16 years old.
In faxed statement on Wednesday the company said it is now developing a computer sofware program to better monitor the hours its teenage employees work.

"Irving Oil Corporation has a long tradition of commitment to Maine's teen-agers through sponsorships and employment opportunities, and this will be continuing in the future," said Chris Mc Auliffe, vice president for company New England operations.
